title: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time's Director Was Chosen For His Ability To "Solve Problems Very Aggressively"
summary:
"This has been a really good experience".

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 gained a new director in HokWai Ng, a developer at Nintendo who started his career with Wii Fit Plus before becoming involved with planning on Tears of the Kingdom for the Switch.

In a new interview with Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi over on Polygon, Aonuma commented on the reason why Ng was chosen to lead the development on Ocarina of Time. He cited Ng's ability to "solve problems very aggressively, very proactively" during his time on Tears of the Kingdom, while his idea for future projects made Aonuma believe that he would be the right fit for a remake.

title: "I'll Leave It To Your Imagination" - Aonuma's Keeping Quiet On Bombchu Girl's Relationship Status
summary:
Alley whoops.

With the Ocarina of Time launching on Switch 2 today, producers Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi have taken part in a series of interviews about the original game, its remakes and their fondest memories of it. All of them have provided a nice read and some fascinating insights into one of our all-time faves, but Game Informer has taken one for the team and asked the question that we all really want to know: what's the situation with the Bombchu Bowling girl?

Most of us will admit to having a little childhood crush on the bowling alley owner when we first played the game, and with the remake bringing everything back to life with its brand-new visual style, we'd wager that it will relight some long-forgotten fires.

title: Guide: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Walkthrough (Switch 2 Remake): Guide To The Main Quest, Side Quests & Collectables
summary:
Your companion to a huge adventure.

Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a dense adventure with many secrets to find, and while the critical path is fairly linear, it's rarely straightforward - asking you to pick up select items and upgrades before you can start exploring its many dungeons.

That's why a Zelda: Ocarina of Time walkthrough comes in handy. Though the Switch 2 version follows the same beats as the N64 original, we'd estimate around 10% of the game's puzzles and locations have been changed or updated - just enough to throw off those very familiar with the 1998 version.
